notes:
User is organizing a crowded shoe closet and plans to sort shoes by type, then by color within each group; out-of-season shoes will go in storage bins. They own brown leather boots with a loose heel and are concerned they may break. Plan: find a local cobbler via reviews/recommendations, get a quote/check leather-repair experience, use a boot-sized cedar shoe tree, and buy a leather-specific cleaning kit (gentle cleaner, conditioner, protector, brush/cloth), testing products first. Brands mentioned: Saphir, Kiwi, Lexol. They also received general advice about gentle cleaning, conditioning, waterproofing, careful storage, and professional maintenance.

They recently bought black Converse Chuck Taylor All Stars and have now worn them six times, most recently running errands yesterday. They love their comfort/versatility and asked about protecting canvas from mud/rain with a compatible waterproofing spray; suggestions included testing discreetly and considering Scotchgard, Crepe Protect, or Nikwax, while checking breathability/appearance. Gentle cleaning advice: mild soap and water, soft brushes/cloths, careful laces/stain treatment, residue removal, air-drying, and waterproofing.

Recommendations included diluted mild soap, microfiber cloths, soft brushing, wiping off residue, air-drying, sneaker-cleaning products for stubborn marks, and avoiding harsh chemicals or abrasives.
